name: Firefly lamp
description: A glass tank with a mesh lid, planted with purple leaves. The giant firefly living inside glows bright enough to see by.
notes: A tank 500 by 320 by 300 mm in a black frame on a bed of soil, with purple and green leaves, a stone, a twig and a giant firefly 170 mm long whose tail is drawn in crystal-glow-white, under a mesh lid with a wire carry handle. The look tiles draw the glass and mesh opaque, so the tank reads as a closed box there; with the front glass hidden the plants and firefly read clearly, and in the game the glass stays see-through. Giving off light and feeding the firefly have no content field yet. Infected usage stands for a survivor's hand-made lamp found in the wasteland; Deadvox may want a survivor tag instead.

name: Forged sheep shears
description: Two hand-forged blades joined by a springy steel bow. Squeeze to cut wool from a sheep, cloth or hide.
notes: Lies along x, 310 mm long: a bow spring at the back, two handles and two leaf blades sprung open, iron-dull for the forged body and steel-bright for the blades. CHECK VOLUME (x0.36): the shears are flat and thin, so their box is smaller than the reference's 750 ml. Shears carry only cutting: shearing waits for livestock shearing, and shears are no butchering blade.

name: Bronze sheep shears
description: Sheep shears cast and hammered from bronze, sprung open by their own bow.
notes: Rides on the forged_shears model with every slot in bronze. The reference weighs it at 900 g against the forged pair's 820 g; set its mass when the drafts are applied.

name: Saddle and bridle
description: A leather riding saddle with stirrups and a wool pad, and a bridle and bit to go with it. Fit it to a tame animal to ride it.
notes: A western saddle 580 mm long, standing on its stirrups: tan skirts, a chestnut seat with a raised cantle and horn, a navy wool pad, wooden stirrups on leathers, cotton cinch straps with steel rings, and a brown bridle coiled on the seat with its bit, a rein hanging from the horn. CHECK VOLUME (x20): the reference's 7 L is far below a real saddle's bulk; the box counts the air under the seat and between the stirrups too. The mass is the reference's 2 kg; a real saddle weighs 10 to 20 kg. Fitting it to an animal has no content field yet.

name: Livestock scale
description: A long steel platform under a ribbed rubber mat, with a digital readout on a cable. Big enough to weigh a horse or a cow, or yourself.
notes: A galvanised deck 1960 by 720 mm on four rubber feet, ribbed black mat, a carry handle at each end and the readout box lying on the mat with a green display and three keys. CHECK VOLUME (x6): the reference's 40 L reads as the steel alone; the drawn deck is solid and 64 mm thick. It is moved rather than fixed, so it has no workstation; weighing has no use in Deadvox yet, so it declares no quality. The size is a placeholder for a thing too long for a pack.

name: Sheep shears
description: Steel blade shears with red plastic grips, sprung open by a bow. Made for shearing wool, they cut cloth and hide as well.
notes: The same shape as forged_shears in bright and stainless steel, with red plastic sleeves over the handles; a separate row because the sleeves are extra pieces. CHECK VOLUME (x0.48): flat and thin, so the box is under the reference's 750 ml.

name: Modified radio
description: A portable radio with its tuning knob pulled off and a tangle of boards, coil and wire taped to its back. Someone rebuilt it for one purpose.
notes: The radio model's case and handle with the tuning knob replaced by a bare shaft, and on the back an aluminium plate, a green circuit board with two chips, a copper coil, a grey tape band and red and yellow wires led over the top. Whatever it was rebuilt to do has no content field yet.

name: Portable radio
description: A battery transistor radio with a carry handle and a fold-down antenna. Turn it on to hear whatever is still broadcasting.
notes: A case 190 by 115 by 50 mm, front on +z: aluminium speaker grille, white tuning scale with a red needle, volume and tuning knobs, a black carry handle and a steel antenna folded along the top. Batteries and receiving broadcasts have no content field yet. The existing portable_radio model is a handheld walkie-talkie shape, so this is its own row.

name: Remote-control car
description: A red toy truck on fat rubber tyres, driven by radio from a hand controller.
notes: A truck 310 mm long and 190 mm wide over its tyres, front on +z: red shell and arches, dark windows, black chassis and bumpers, white lamps, four treaded tyres with aluminium hubs and a whip antenna at the back. CHECK VOLUME (x9.6): the antenna doubles the box height and the reference's 1.5 L is small for a car this size. The controller is not drawn; it would be its own item. Driving it has no content field yet.
